commands.name: align.auto
commands.title: Auto-align the part
commands.description: Read a coordinate system off the scan and apply it, as Auto-align then Confirm alignment do: the directions most faces are square to and the axis round walls run along, the part standing on its base, its long side along X. level: settled (the default) lays all the faces on the axes at once, by area; largest squares the largest flat face exactly and settles the rest about its normal. Returns what the pose was read from, the transform, how many elements moved, and square — how square it came out: largest (the largest flat face’s axis, area, tiltDeg) and per axis the faces square to it with their tilts. Trap: a drafted wall reads as its draft, not as an alignment error. One undo step.

level.description: settled (the default): all faces at once, by area. largest: the largest flat face exactly, the rest settled about its normal.

detail.description: brief (the default): the transform and how many elements moved. full: every element where it now is.

commands.name: align.clear
commands.title: Reset the alignment
commands.description: Put the part back in the coordinates the scanner delivered it in, with everything measured on it. Returns how many elements moved with it. One undo step.

detail.description: brief (the default): the transform and how many elements moved. full: every element where it now is.

commands.name: align.datum
commands.title: Align the part to datums
commands.description: A 3-2-1 alignment, as the panel’s alignment box sets it up: primary levels the part — a plane (or 3 points) whose outward normal becomes primaryAxis (default z-); secondary turns it — a line or axis (or 2 points) laid along secondaryAxis (default x+), or a plane; origin is the zero point — a point, sphere or circle (or 1 point). Elements by id or name, or points in mm used as given, not snapped. Trap: a plane as secondary puts its outward NORMAL on secondaryAxis, not its face along it. Each datum zeroes the coordinates it owns, the origin only those left open; an origin alone moves without turning. On a first alignment the coordinates nothing sets are centred on the scan’s box (keepFree: true leaves them). Returns the transform applied, how many elements moved, centred, origin { set, at, note } and parallelFace when a face parallel to the levelling plane within 5 mm holds more of the scan. One undo step.

points.description: 3 points, mm — they span the face.

primary.description: Levelling: an element, or 3 points on the scan.

primaryAxis.description: The axis the primary’s outward normal becomes; default z-.

points.description: 2 points, mm — they run along the edge.

secondary.description: Rotation: an element, or 2 points on the scan.

secondaryAxis.description: The axis the secondary runs along (a plane: its normal); default x+.

element.description: An element for the zero point.

point.description: A point for the zero point, mm.

origin.description: The zero point: an element, or a point on the scan.

keepFree.description: First alignment: leave the coordinates nothing sets where they are instead of centring.

detail.description: brief (the default): the transform and how many elements moved. full: every element where it now is.

commands.name: align.symmetry
commands.title: Align the part on its symmetry plane
commands.description: Settle the part’s pose on its mirror plane and apply it, as Use symmetry then Confirm alignment do: the pose is Auto-align’s, the mirror plane a measured symmetry plane or one searched for on the scan; the axis nearest its normal is turned onto it and the zero point put on it. Refuses when the scan has no symmetry plane. Returns the note on what it settled on, the transform and how many elements moved. One undo step.

detail.description: brief (the default): the transform and how many elements moved. full: every element where it now is.

commands.name: deviation.align
commands.title: Best-fit the scan onto the reference
commands.description: Rigid best fit (no scale) of the scan onto the reference part, then the deviation map under it. mode auto (the default) finds the pose on its own; points starts from three or more pairs of corresponding points (scan and reference, mm) then refines; local refines the fit in hand on a marked surface only (vertices), within searchDistance mm. Returns the alignment (RMS, points matched, transform) and the map’s statistics. One undo step.

reference.description: The same point on the reference, mm.

vertices.description: local: the surface to refine on, scan vertex numbers.

searchDistance.description: local: how far a point may lie from the reference to count, mm.

commands.name: deviation.export
commands.title: Export the deviation as data
commands.description: The deviation map as a file of readings, for working on it elsewhere: side "scan" (the default) a reading per scan vertex with its signed distance from the reference (or the element measured against), side "reference" a reading per sample on the reference; format ply (the default, binary), npy (N × 4 float32 x, y, z, d) or csv. Returns the file with readings, measured, withinTolerance, withinTolerancePct, tolerance and searchDistance. Trap: the distance is NaN where there is no reading, and a reading past the search distance is kept as it is — |d| ≤ searchDistance says it counts. Changes nothing.

side.description: The readings: per scan vertex (the default), or per sample on the reference.

commands.name: deviation.hotspots
commands.title: Where the deviation lies over tolerance
commands.description: The deviation map read as patches: the vertices past the tolerance gathered into connected regions, the largest and farthest first — where the part is off, how large each place is and by how much. Needs a map (deviation.align or deviation.set_target). Returns each patch’s centroid, box, area, count, mean, extreme, depth, volume, kind ("feature": material missing or misplaced, to model or name; "texture": roughness), side, the extreme’s point and vertex, a few vertices, and onReference; features, found, over and unmeasured; on: "reference" reads the map on the reference, adding noScan. Trap: read far every time — the vertices past the search distance, which the map draws bare: far.inside is scan deep inside the reference (a hole, pocket or slot the model lacks), far.outside scan standing off it. Changes nothing.

tolerance.description: ± mm; the map’s tolerance by default.

patches.description: How many patches to name; 8 by default, 50 at most.

grain.description: mm two vertices over tolerance may lie apart and be one patch; three point spacings by default.

on.description: The map read: on the scan (the default) or on the reference.

commands.name: deviation.measure
commands.title: Measure the deviation map
commands.description: Measure the deviation map again under the alignment in hand — after a change of facing limit or search distance, say. deviation.align measures it already. Returns the map’s statistics (min, max, mean, RMS, sigma, share within the tolerance, points matched). One undo step.

commands.name: deviation.open_reference
commands.title: Open the reference part
commands.description: Open the nominal part the scan is compared with — STEP from CAD, or STL, PLY, OBJ or 3MF — in place of the one there is; any alignment and map against the old one go, the elements measured on the scan stay. Returns the deviation state. Not undoable: a new reference starts a new history.

name.description: The file's name with its extension — "bracket.step".

units.description: The file’s units: mm (the default), cm, m or in. Everything is measured in mm once read.

commands.name: deviation.set_target
commands.title: Measure against an element
commands.description: Map how far the scan strays from one of its own fitted elements — a plane, cylinder, cone, sphere or torus — instead of from a reference part; null goes back to the reference. side is the material side, read off the scan when the element is chosen (outward: the element’s outer side; inward: a bore or shell) — give it to override. facingDeg limits which surface counts to what faces the element within that many degrees, null for any. Needs the viewport. Returns the map’s statistics. One undo step.

side.description: The material side; read off the scan by default.

facingDeg.description: The facing limit, degrees, or null for any.

commands.name: deviation.settings
commands.title: Set how the deviation is read
commands.description: The deviation map’s reading: range (colour scale, ± mm), maxDistance (search distance, mm), bands, tolerance (± mm the statistics count within), facingDeg (a change measures the map again), colormap (the person’s own choice, kept outside the undo — read settings.colormap for the ramp before judging a picture), on (which surface a map against the reference is painted on; read both sides) and show (the map switch; false leaves the surface bare, the map still measured). Returns the deviation state. Trap: the map paints in the Deviation workspace only — workspace.set deviation brings it back, and view.render says which map it painted (map) or why none (mapWhy). One undo step.

bands.description: Stepped colours, or null for smooth.

colormap.description: jet (blue inside, green on the surface, red outside) or a perceptual ramp.

on.description: The surface the map is painted on; scan by default.

show.description: The map painted (true) or the surface left bare (false).

commands.name: deviation.volume
commands.title: Volume error
commands.description: The scan and the reference part compared as solids, on a grid of small cells: each cell inside one and not the other is an error, touching cells a region. Read it before the surface patches — it tells how much material is wrong and where, which the nearest-point map cannot: excess is material the reference has and the part has not, missing the other way round, unsure where the scan does not say (never an error). Needs deviation.align. Returns totals (mm³ and % of the reference) and the regions largest first, each with kind, volume, maxDepth, thickness, shape (layer or lump), centroid, deepest, box, evidence and confidence. Trap: nothing thinner than smallestSeen (two cells) is seen — the surface map stays the tool for fine offsets. About 15 s on a 1.5M-triangle scan. Changes nothing kept.

tolerance.description: ± mm; the map’s tolerance by default.

cell.description: The cell, mm; by default half the tolerance or a 250th of the reference’s longest side, the larger.

regions.description: How many regions to name; 8 by default, 50 at most.

within.description: Only this box is looked at, in the reference’s frame.

kinds.description: Only regions of these kinds named; all by default. The totals are of all.

commands.name: dimension.add
commands.title: Add a dimension
commands.description: Measure between elements, or a size or tolerance of one, as the panel’s dimension box does. refs are the elements by id or name, in slot order (a section counts as the plane it was cut on). Without type, the type follows the elements as clicking them does — two planes their distance, a plane and an axis theirs, and so on; with type, one of dist-point-point, dist-point-axis, dist-point-plane, dist-axis-axis, dist-axis-plane, dist-plane-plane, angle-axis-axis, angle-axis-plane, angle-plane-plane, size-diameter, form-flatness, form-cylindricity, form-circularity, form-sphericity, orient-parallelism, orient-perpendicularity, orient-angularity, loc-coaxiality (the measure-reference guide lists each one’s slots). anchor, for two spheres: center (default), gap or span; limit holds the value to a ceiling or a nominal ± band. Returns the dimension with its value (mm or degrees, finer than the panel shows), the formatted value and the verdict. One undo step.

type.description: The dimension type — see the description.

anchor.description: Two spheres: centre to centre (the default), the gap between them, or the span across them.

max.description: The most the value may be, mm or degrees.

kind.description: A nominal with an allowance either side.

nominal.description: The nominal value, mm or degrees.

limit.description: What the value is checked against, for a pass or fail verdict.

commands.name: dimension.remove
commands.title: Delete a dimension
commands.description: Delete a dimension or tolerance. One undo step.

commands.name: dimension.set_basic
commands.title: Set an angularity’s basic angle
commands.description: The basic angle an angularity tolerance is read against, in degrees, or null to take it off. One undo step.

commands.name: dimension.set_limit
commands.title: Set a dimension’s limit
commands.description: Hold a dimension to a limit — a ceiling, or a nominal ± band — or take it off with null. Returns the dimension with its verdict. One undo step.

max.description: The most the value may be, mm or degrees.

kind.description: A nominal with an allowance either side.

nominal.description: The nominal value, mm or degrees.

oneOf.description: What the value is checked against, for a pass or fail verdict.

limit.description: The limit, or null for none.

commands.name: element.construct
commands.title: Construct an element
commands.description: Construct an element from others and typed-in numbers, as the panel’s creation methods do — point: point-coords, point-centroid, point-midpoint, point-line-plane; line: line-two-points, line-axis, line-plane-plane; plane: plane-three-points, plane-offset, plane-midplane, plane-coords, plane-symmetry; circle: circle-plane-cylinder, circle-plane-sphere, circle-coords. refs fill the slots in order, by id or name (a section stands in a plane’s slot as its cut plane; "XY", "YZ", "XZ" become plane elements, listed under made); params are the numbers in order or by key. point-centroid and plane-symmetry measure the scan (vertices confines them, seed starts the symmetry search), plane-symmetry answering symmetry { rms, matched, sampled }. Returns the element. One undo step.

method.description: The creation method — see the description.

items.description: A source element; in a plane’s slot also a section or "XY", "YZ", "XZ".

refs.description: The method’s source elements, slot by slot.

oneOf.description: The numbers in the method’s order.
The numbers by key (x, y, z; offset; nx, ny, nz, px, py, pz; d, cx, cy, cz).

seed.description: plane-symmetry: the plane the search starts from.

vertices.description: point-centroid, plane-symmetry: only these scan vertices.

assumed.description: The designed diameter, mm: drawn and exported at it, reported as measured.

to.description: A plane element, a section, or "XY", "YZ", "XZ".

relation.description: normal (the default): the direction is the plane’s normal. inPlane: it lies in the plane.

orient.description: Align the direction to a plane, as designed; the measured fit is kept beside it.

name.description: A name; else numbered by kind — "Sphere 2".

commands.name: element.fit
commands.title: Fit an element
commands.description: Fit an element on the scan where the panel would take a click: a plane, sphere, cylinder, cone or torus grows its surface from the place (or places) in at and is best-fitted to it; a point is the place itself; a circle goes through three or more places, or round an open rim (rim, numbered by scan.qa). A place is { vertex } or { point: [x, y, z] } (mm, current frame; the nearest vertex is taken). Trap: a seed near an edge can land on the wrong surface — say what is sought with side, radius, axis or within, and surfaces that do not match are passed over. Returns the element with its fit, the seeds used (inRegion, offMm, deg), the region grown (area, box, normalSpreadDeg, fill, sagitta) and a warning when the points look like two surfaces, a bore steps or is closed at an end, or a plane is a bead’s crown — the measure-reference guide (Elements) says how to read each. One undo step.

point.description: [x, y, z] mm in the current frame; the nearest scan vertex is taken.

screen.description: A viewport pixel [x, y] (not available yet).

candidate.description: A feature from scan.candidates (not available yet).

point.description: [x, y, z] mm in the current frame; the nearest scan vertex is taken.

screen.description: A viewport pixel [x, y] (not available yet).

candidate.description: A feature from scan.candidates (not available yet).

side.description: Sphere, cylinder, cone: inside (concave, a bore) or outside (convex, a shaft).

radius.description: Sphere, cylinder, cone: the radius range sought.

axis.description: Cylinder, cone: the axis direction, roughly (within 20°).

within.description: The surface stays inside this box.

mark.description: Leave the grown region marked for element.fit_marked.

rim.description: Circle: an open rim of the scan by its scan.qa number, in place of at.

sigma.description: Outlier cut-off, sigma: 3 (the default), 2, 1, or 0 for all points.

knownDiameter.description: Sphere: a known diameter held, mm (a gauge ball); the centre alone is fitted.

assumed.description: The designed diameter, mm: drawn and exported at it, reported as measured.

to.description: A plane element, a section, or "XY", "YZ", "XZ".

relation.description: normal (the default): the direction is the plane’s normal. inPlane: it lies in the plane.

orient.description: Align the direction to a plane, as designed; the measured fit is kept beside it.

start.description: Cylinder: mm past the start (negative pulls it in).

uMin.description: Plane: mm past the edge along its first axis.

extend.description: Mm a cylinder or plane is drawn and exported past the measured surface.

name.description: A name; else numbered by kind — "Sphere 2".

commands.name: element.fit_marked
commands.title: Fit an element to a marked surface
commands.description: Fit a plane, sphere, cylinder, cone or torus to exactly the scan vertices given, with no search for the surface — vertices, or marked: true for the points the last element.fit { mark: true }, scan.segment { mark } or scan.query { mark: true } left marked, or box (with normal: only those facing a way) for every vertex inside it. The element keeps the marking as its recipe. Returns the element, and with box how many points it took. One undo step.

vertices.description: The scan vertices of the surface.

marked.description: The points left marked, in place of vertices.

box.description: The scan inside a box, in place of vertices.

normal.description: With box: only the vertices facing this way.

sigma.description: Outlier cut-off, sigma: 3 (the default), 2, 1, or 0 for all points.

knownDiameter.description: Sphere: a known diameter held, mm (a gauge ball); the centre alone is fitted.

assumed.description: The designed diameter, mm: drawn and exported at it, reported as measured.

to.description: A plane element, a section, or "XY", "YZ", "XZ".

relation.description: normal (the default): the direction is the plane’s normal. inPlane: it lies in the plane.

orient.description: Align the direction to a plane, as designed; the measured fit is kept beside it.

start.description: Cylinder: mm past the start (negative pulls it in).

uMin.description: Plane: mm past the edge along its first axis.

extend.description: Mm a cylinder or plane is drawn and exported past the measured surface.

name.description: A name; else numbered by kind — "Sphere 2".

commands.name: element.remove
commands.title: Delete an element
commands.description: Delete an element — and with it every construction built on it and every dimension on any of them. Returns what went. One undo step.

commands.name: element.rename
commands.title: Rename an element
commands.description: Give an element another name; dimensions and constructions on it keep pointing at it. One undo step.

commands.name: element.set_visible
commands.title: Show or hide elements
commands.description: Show or hide one element, or all of them with all: true. A hidden element still measures; only its drawing and surface tint go. One undo step.

commands.name: export.cloud
commands.title: Export the scan as a point cloud
commands.description: Every scan vertex with its normal, in the pose it is shown in, as a binary PLY (the default) or an XYZ text file. Needs the viewport. Returns the file’s bytes and the name the panel would save it under.

commands.name: export.csv
commands.title: Export the 2D measurements as CSV
commands.description: The 2D Measure elements and dimensions as CSV, for a spreadsheet. Returns the file’s bytes and the name the panel would save it under.

commands.name: export.dxf
commands.title: Export the 2D sheet as DXF
commands.description: The 2D sheet as DXF for CAD — millimetres, y up, the origin on the sheet’s alignment, the edges thinned to a sketch’s worth. Needs the browser. Returns the file’s bytes and the name the panel would save it under.

commands.name: export.step
commands.title: Export the elements as STEP
commands.description: The measured elements as analytic STEP geometry for CAD — as drawn, extensions and assumed diameters included — and, in a group per section, what was measured on the sections. style: solids (the default: solids and faces) or surfaces (construction surfaces), remembered as the panel’s choice. Returns the file’s bytes and the name the panel would save it under.

commands.name: export.stl
commands.title: Export the scan as a mesh
commands.description: The scan as a binary STL — or, format 3mf, a 3MF in millimetres with the scan’s own colours — in the pose it is shown in, a datum alignment and a best fit onto the reference included. Needs the viewport. Returns the file’s bytes and the name the panel would save it under.

commands.name: export.svg
commands.title: Export the 2D sheet as SVG
commands.description: The 2D sheet at true scale as SVG — the shown edges and the visible elements, aligned and turned as shown — for a vector editor, a laser or a 1:1 print. Needs the browser. Returns the file’s bytes and the name the panel would save it under.

commands.name: flat.calibrate
commands.title: Calibrate the image
commands.description: Set the image’s scale against a known length, as the Calibrate tool does: distance takes two places a known distance apart, diameter three or more on a circle of known diameter; mm is that length. Every measurement follows the new scale, and the edges are found again (their chain numbers change). Returns the calibration. One undo step.

mode.description: distance (two places) or diameter (three or more on a circle).

items.description: A place on the sheet, [x, y] in the sheet’s units.

points.description: The places, in the sheet’s units as they are now.

commands.name: flat.detect_edges
commands.title: Detect the image’s edges
commands.description: Find the edges in the image again at a sensitivity from 0 (only the strongest) to 1 (every faint one) — what the edge methods of flat.fit and the snapping of every place follow. The chains are numbered afresh. Needs the browser. Returns how many edge chains were found.

commands.name: flat.dimension_add
commands.title: Add a 2D dimension
commands.description: Measure between two 2D elements: flat-dist-point-point (point, point), flat-dist-point-line (point, line), flat-dist-line-line (line, line), flat-angle-line-line (line, line). Points, circles and arcs count as their point (centre), lines as lines. Without type, the first that takes the two elements in the order given. Returns the dimensions on the sheet. One undo step.

commands.name: flat.edges
commands.title: List the detected edges
commands.description: The edge chains detected on the sheet, by number — what flat.fit takes as chains. Each with its length, whether it closes, its point count and box, in the sheet’s units; the longest first, or with near the nearest first (each with its nearest point and distance; within reach only, when given). box keeps the chains that enter it, minLength the long ones. tolerance adds each chain’s polyline thinned to that (5000 points at most over all). limit chains at most, 50 by default. Trap: the numbers change when the edges are found again. Changes nothing.

box.description: Only chains with a point in this box.

reach.description: With near: only chains this close.

minLength.description: Only chains at least this long.

tolerance.description: Add each chain’s polyline, thinned to this.

commands.name: flat.edit
commands.title: Change a 2D element, dimension, note or count
commands.description: Change one thing on the 2D sheet, by id or name: an element, a dimension or a count takes a new name; a note new text or a new place (at, its lower-left corner); any of them visible: false to leave it out of the stage, the picture and the exports. Returns the 2D state. One undo step.

commands.name: flat.fit
commands.title: Fit a 2D element
commands.description: Make a 2D element on the sheet as its tool does — kind point, line, circle, arc or spline, by a method of that kind: point: flat-point-pick (pick), flat-point-midpoint (construct), flat-point-intersect (construct), flat-point-center (construct); line: flat-line-pick (pick), flat-line-seed (seed), flat-line-edge (edge); circle: flat-circle-pick (pick), flat-circle-seed (seed), flat-circle-edge (edge), flat-circle-centers (construct); arc: flat-arc-pick (pick), flat-arc-edge (edge); spline: flat-spline-pick (pick). A pick method takes points, the places clicked (snapped to the nearest edge within reach unless snap: false; picks says where each landed); a seed method one place on an edge and grows along it; an edge method a place on an edge taken whole, or chains and box; a construct method refs, other 2D elements. Returns the element with its fit. One undo step.

method.description: The method — see the description; the kind’s first pick method by default.

items.description: A place on the sheet, [x, y] in the sheet’s units.

points.description: The places, in the sheet’s units.

chains.description: Edge chains by number, taken whole (edge or seed methods).

box.description: Edge points inside this box, sheet units (edge or seed methods).

snap.description: Picks snap to the nearest edge within reach; true by default.

reach.description: How far a place reaches for an edge, sheet units; ten image pixels by default.

commands.name: flat.note_add
commands.title: Write a note on the sheet
commands.description: Write a text note on the 2D sheet, as the Text tool does — one line, a line break written as " / "; at is its lower-left corner, sheet units. It is drawn on the stage and in flat.render, written into the SVG and DXF exports and listed in the report. Returns the note with its id. One undo step.

commands.name: flat.objects
commands.title: Find the parts on the image
commands.description: The separate parts on the flatbed image, parted from the background by a grey level (Otsu’s unless threshold is given) and numbered in reading order — what flat.profile takes by number. Returns each with area, holes, box, centroid, equivalentDiameter, feret (largest and smallest caliper widths with their directions), axisAngle, chains (the edge chains along its outline) and, with outline, its polygon. Trap: minArea drops smaller ones, 1 mm² by default. Changes nothing.

dark.description: The parts are darker than the background.

minArea.description: The smallest part, in the sheet’s units squared.

outline.description: Add each outline, thinned to this, in the sheet’s units.

commands.name: flat.open_image
commands.title: Open a flatbed image
commands.description: Open a flatbed scan of a part — PNG or JPEG, at the highest optical resolution — on the 2D sheet, in place of the image there was. The scale it declares about itself is taken until it is calibrated. Needs the browser. Returns the 2D state. Not undoable: a new image starts a new history.

name.description: The file's name with its extension — "part.png".

commands.name: flat.profile
commands.title: Profile an outline and count its peaks
commands.description: An outline read against a centre (radial, the default: a part seen from above) or along an axis (axial: a part lying on its side, each side apart), and its peaks counted — the teeth of a knurl or a gear. The outline is an object of the last flat.objects by number, or edge chains by number; about is the element it is read about, else the outline’s own centre or long axis. Returns per side the count, pitch, envelope (max, min, mean peak, mean valley; radial also as diameters) and every peak’s position; points adds the sampled profile. Trap: a peak must stand prominence above the higher valley either side (0.3 of the profile’s spread by default). mark: true puts a count on the sheet — one undo step; otherwise nothing changes.

object.description: An object of the last flat.objects, by number.

chains.description: Edge chains by number, as one outline.

about.description: A circle, arc or point (radial), or a line (axial).

axis.description: Without about: radial about the outline’s centre (the default), or axial along its long axis.

samples.description: Bins round the turn or along the axis; from the point count by default.

prominence.description: How far a peak must stand out, sheet units.

mark.description: Put a count on every peak.

commands.name: flat.remove
commands.title: Remove from the 2D sheet
commands.description: Remove elements, dimensions, notes and counts from the 2D sheet, each by id or name (a note by id) — all of them or none. An element built on a removed one stays and says it has lost its source, a dimension on one turns invalid; the answer names them. Returns what is left. One undo step.

commands.name: flat.render
commands.title: Picture the sheet
commands.description: A picture of the 2D sheet as a PNG, as the sheet lies in its own units — +X right, +Y up, whatever the alignment or turns — with a grid and its values along the top and left edges. map says where it lies: picture pixel (column c, row r from the top) is the sheet place [left + c·unitsPerPx, top − r·unitsPerPx]. frame zooms in on a box. show puts layers in or out: image, edges (the detected chains), chains (their numbers), elements (with counts and the alignment), dimensions, notes, labels, grid. 800 px on the long side by default, up to 2048. Needs the browser.

frame.description: What to picture, in the sheet’s units — the whole sheet by default.

commands.name: flat.report
commands.title: Get the 2D report
commands.description: The 2D Measure report as its Copy button gives it: the image or section, the scale it rests on, the alignment, every element, dimension, count and note.

commands.name: flat.set_alignment
commands.title: Align the sheet
commands.description: Put the part’s zero point at origin and its X axis through xAxis, as the Align tool’s two clicks do: the report, the panel and the exports then read in that frame. Places given to the commands stay the sheet’s own. clear: true takes the alignment off. Returns the 2D state. One undo step.

origin.description: The zero point, in the sheet’s units.

commands.name: guide.read
commands.title: Read a guide
commands.description: How to do a task with ScanRuler: the workflow, the judgement and the traps the tools’ own descriptions do not carry, written for this build — read the guide for your task, whole, before its first step, and a section again when you need it. The guides: measure — measuring a 3D scan: fitting elements, dimensions and GD&T-like checks, sections and the 2D sheet, deviation against a reference part, wall thickness, the report — by hand or as an automatic run over many scans; measure-reference — the measuring tools’ shapes with examples, what each answer costs, what each refusal means — a section at a time, as the measure guide sends you. topic: a guide, or several read in order (a guide and the ones it is read with, in one call) — as many as fit in about 80 k characters, the rest named in next, to read in the next call. A guide longer than that by itself answers its sections in order while they fit, and names the rest in sectionsLeft, each to read by section. A guide’s sections for one moment of the task — measuring, building — are not in the whole read: later names each with when to read it, and the note says how; read it by section when that moment comes, before the step it is for. section: one section of one guide, by its heading — the index lists them, with when to read those a whole read leaves for later. A long section with ### parts under it — a reference’s list of command shapes — is best read by those parts: section takes a ### heading too, the one part you need. With no topic, the index: each guide with its sections and what each costs in tokens. Changes nothing.

topic.description: A guide by its id, or several to read in order — as many as fit in one answer, the rest named in next. Leave it out for the index.

section.description: One section of the guide, by its heading — a ## section or a ### part of one (without its number, or a part of it that names one section), whole: a section the whole read named in later, when its moment comes, or one to read again. Only with one topic.

commands.name: history.checkpoint
commands.title: Mark the history
commands.description: Mark where the undo history stands, before a run of changes that should stand or fall together: history.restore { checkpoint } later undoes every step made since, back to this mark. Changes nothing. Returns the checkpoint, the step on top and how many there are.

commands.name: history.redo
commands.title: Redo
commands.description: Redo the step undone last. Returns the step’s name and the session afterwards in brief (detail "full": the whole of it).

detail.description: brief (the default): what the steps change, in brief, as after; full: the whole session, as state.

commands.name: history.restore
commands.title: Back to a mark in the history
commands.description: Undo every step made since history.checkpoint gave this checkpoint, newest first — a run of changes that went wrong in the middle taken back whole. Refused, undoing nothing, when the mark is gone: undone past it, or the history started afresh (a scan or project opened). Returns the steps undone, newest first, and the session afterwards.

detail.description: brief (the default): what the steps change, in brief, as after; full: the whole session, as state.

commands.name: history.undo
commands.title: Undo
commands.description: Undo the last step — one of the person’s or one of these commands, each of which is one step. Returns the step’s name and the session afterwards in brief (detail "full": the whole of it).

detail.description: brief (the default): what the steps change, in brief, as after; full: the whole session, as state.

commands.name: project.load
commands.title: Open a project
commands.description: Open a .scanruler project in place of the session — its models, then every measurement in it, remeasured, each fit as it was saved. Refuses while the session holds measurements unless discard is true. Needs the browser. Returns the session. Not undoable: an opened project starts a new history.

name.description: Its name, for the status line.

discard.description: true: replace the session though it holds measurements (lost unless saved as a project first). Refused otherwise when there is work to lose.

commands.name: project.rename
commands.title: Name the project
commands.description: Give the project a name — what Save Project saves it under, the stem of every export and the browser tab’s title, kept in the project file. An empty name takes it off, and the scan’s or the image’s name stands in again. session.state reads it as project.name.

name.description: The name; empty takes it off.

commands.name: project.save
commands.title: Save the project
commands.description: The session as a .scanruler project file, as Save Project downloads it: the scan, the reference, the image and every measurement, each rebuilt when it is opened. Needs the browser. Returns the file’s bytes and its name, holds (what is in it, counted — read it before calling the file a revision: a page reset holds no model), aligned (whether the scan stands in an aligned frame) and says (what a workspace wants said of the work saved).

commands.name: report.get
commands.title: Get the report
commands.description: The measurement report. format "text" is word for word what the workspace’s Copy report button gives — measure (elements and dimensions with verdicts), deviation, thickness or flat (2D). format "json" (the default) is the whole session’s report structured: what the numbers rest on (units, scale, frame, alignment, fit method, outlier cut-offs), every element with its fit, every dimension with value, unit, limit and verdict, the tally of checks, the sections, and the deviation, thickness and 2D results with their settings.

workspace.description: For text: whose report — measure (the default), deviation, thickness or flat.

commands.name: scan.draft
commands.title: Read the draft against a pull
commands.description: The scan’s walls that run near a pull direction — the sides a mould opens along — gathered into patches, each with draftDeg, the angle it leans off the pull: positive where the wall faces partly along the pull, negative where it faces back (a back draft, an undercut); with sigmaDeg, spreadDeg, centroid, box, area (mm²), count, facing, turnDeg and round for a boss’s or hole’s round side. Needs pull; box, nearDeg (10), patches (12), minArea (1 mm²) and split (a plane no patch reaches across: "symmetry", a plane element, "XY", "YZ", "XZ" or { point, normal }) narrow it. Trap: read it early on a moulded or cast part, along each direction the tools open — walls that lean half a degree to a few explain fits that miss by the lean. Changes nothing.

box.description: Only the scan inside this box.

split.description: Keep every patch to one side of this plane.

commands.name: scan.fit_surface
commands.title: Fit a sloped or curved patch
commands.description: A patch of the scan measured as a surface — a sloped side, a twisted ruled face, a dome, a saddle — from vertices or a box (normal keeps those facing a way). Returns the patch’s frame (origin, normal, basisU, basisV) and each model as a height over (u, v): plane (a + b·u + c·v), bilinear (+ d·u·v) and quadric (+ d·u² + e·u·v + f·v², with curvature { k1, k2, r1, r2, axis1, axis2, shape }), each with coefficients, rms and worst; model: best (the default) fits every one and names the simplest whose rms is within a tenth of the lowest. Trap: 7 points at least, at most limit (20000) spread evenly. Changes nothing.

vertices.description: The scan vertices of the patch.

box.description: The scan inside a box, in place of vertices.

normal.description: With box: only the vertices facing this way.

model.description: Which surface; best (the default) fits each and names the simplest that holds.

limit.description: How many points at most; 20000 by default.

commands.name: scan.heightmap
commands.title: Map the scan’s heights
commands.description: Where the scan is first met looking along an axis (axis, -z by default: the top surface from above) or square onto a plane (plane: an element, "XY", "YZ", "XZ", or { origin, normal, u? }), over a grid of cells: pocket floors, ledges, a step's height, a face's tilt, a pad's tiers, an icon on a key in one call. of: height (the default), deviation (the map's reading where each ray lands) or relief (the height less the surface round it, for icons, grooves and lettering). Returns cell, origin [u0, v0], cols, rows, grid (rows of mm from the low v up, null where nothing; grid[r][c] stands at u0 + (c + ½)·cell, v0 + (r + ½)·cell), min, max, hit, valued; with plane also its frame (a cell's point is origin + u·U + v·V + height·normal). levels: true gives the values gathered into levels in place of the grid; picture: true adds the map coloured. Trap: with plane, box is [u, v, height] in the plane's frame (or { world }), and scanLies says where the scan lies when few cells meet it. Changes nothing.

min.description: Lowest corner, mm ([u, v, height] with plane).

max.description: Highest corner, mm ([u, v, height] with plane).

world.description: A box in the world, in place of min and max.

box.description: The part looked at; the scan’s box by default. With plane: [u, v, height], or world: { min, max }.

axis.description: The way looked: -z (the default) from above, +z from below, ±x, ±y.

origin.description: A point on the plane, mm.

normal.description: Its normal: the side looked from.

u.description: A direction for u, flattened into the plane; a sketch’s by default.

plane.description: Look square onto this plane instead of along an axis.

flip.description: With plane: look from its other side.

of.description: height (the default), deviation (the map’s, where the ray lands) or relief (height less the surface round it).

smooth.description: relief: the smoothing sigma, mm; three cells by default.

grid.description: The grid of numbers (the default unless levels); false returns the picture alone.

levels.description: Gather the values into levels, largest first, in place of the grid.

gap.description: levels: the least gap between two levels, mm.

slopeDeg.description: levels of a height: cells steeper are left out, degrees; 10 by default, 90 keeps every one.

picture.description: Add a picture of the map with a scale.

commands.name: scan.nearest
commands.title: Find a place on the scan
commands.description: Where a place lands on the scan: the vertex (a point snaps to the nearest), its coordinates and outward normal, a triangle it is a corner of, and how far it lies from the point asked about. Use it to check a point lies on the surface before fitting there.

point.description: [x, y, z] mm in the current frame; the nearest scan vertex is taken.

screen.description: A viewport pixel [x, y] (not available yet).

candidate.description: A feature from scan.candidates (not available yet).

commands.name: scan.open
commands.title: Open a scan
commands.description: Open a mesh as the scan to measure — STL, PLY, OBJ or 3MF, or a STEP part cut into triangles — in place of the one there is; everything measured on the old one goes with it, so it refuses while the session holds measurements unless discard is true (the refusal names what is held). A reference part opened from a file stays, its alignment and maps gone (referenceKept); one made from the session’s own work goes (referenceDropped). Returns the scan: name, units, vertex and triangle counts, bounding box, centre and diagonal (size), mm. Not undoable: a new scan starts a new history.

name.description: The file's name with its extension — "ballbar.stl".

units.description: The file’s units: mm (the default), cm, m or in. Everything is measured in mm once read.

discard.description: true: replace the session though it holds measurements (lost unless saved as a project first). Refused otherwise when there is work to lose.

commands.name: scan.outline
commands.title: Read the scan’s outline
commands.description: The scan’s outline seen along an axis, or square onto a plane, read as a sketch would draw it: a flange’s plan, a bezel’s opening, a gasket’s shape — each loop as the fewest lines and arcs that follow it within tolerance (mm, 0.2 by default), a round loop as one circle. axis, plane, flip and box as scan.heightmap takes them, u, v as it lays them. Returns loops, the largest first (4 by default): hole, area (mm²), box, points ([u, v] corners), rounds { at, radius, center }, arcs { from, radius, center } or circle { center, radius, rms }, and worst (mm the trace strays from what is drawn, worstAt when past the tolerance). Changes nothing.

axis.description: The way looked: -z (the default) from above, and so on.

origin.description: A point on the plane, mm.

normal.description: Its normal: the side looked from.

u.description: A direction for u, flattened into the plane.

plane.description: Look square onto this plane instead of along an axis.

flip.description: With plane: look from its other side.

min.description: Lowest corner, mm ([u, v, height] with plane).

max.description: Highest corner, mm ([u, v, height] with plane).

world.description: A box in the world, in place of min and max.

box.description: Only the scan inside it; the whole scan by default. With plane: [u, v, height], or world: { min, max }.

tolerance.description: How closely the sketch follows the outline, mm; 0.2 by default.

loops.description: How many loops, the largest first; 4 by default.

commands.name: scan.pattern
commands.title: Count the repeats round an axis
commands.description: Rotational repeats about an axis — a fan's blades, a flange's holes, a wheel's spokes, a gear's teeth — counted from the scan: it is cut square to the axis at each height in at, and each cut (between radius.min and radius.max) is turned against itself. Needs axis: a cylinder, cone, line or circle element, "X", "Y", "Z", or { origin, dir }. Returns per height count, pitchDeg, phaseDeg, betweenDeg (angles as section.cut { across: { axis, angleDeg } } takes them), score (0 to 1; under 0.5 count is 1 and tried says the best), rms, worst, instances (each angleDeg, radius, offDeg, rms, worst, share) and rings (round outlines about the axis: radius, off, towardDeg, rms). Trap: features at different heights and radii need a cut through each, radius kept to one ring. Changes nothing.

oneOf.description: A cylinder, cone, line or circle element, or a coordinate axis "X", "Y", "Z".

origin.description: A point on the axis, mm.

axis.description: The axis the copies repeat round.

oneOf.description: A world point, mm: the height of its foot on the axis.

at.description: Heights to cut at; 6 spread over the scan by default.

radius.description: Only the cut between these distances from the axis.

maxCount.description: The most copies looked for; 60 by default.

instances.description: List each copy; true by default.

commands.name: scan.qa
commands.title: Check the scan before modelling
commands.description: One call before modelling, to know what the scan will and will not give. Returns rims (the open edges of its holes: count, total length, the longest few with rim number, centre, size and circle where one fits — element.fit { kind: "circle", rim } makes it an element), noise (the median scatter of small plane fits, mm; near 0 is a CAD tessellation), thickness through the part along axis (p5, p50, p95, the main faces’ tiltDeg and faces { topDeg, bottomDeg }) and notes, what looks wrong, plainly. Trap: a scanned skin with no rims, or only pinholes, is a wrap bridging the holes it did not see through. Changes nothing.

commands.name: scan.query
commands.title: Read the scan’s points
commands.description: The scan’s vertices inside a box, or within a radius of a point (near), with their outward normals — the points on a face, to measure a dimension or a draft off; normal keeps only those facing a direction. Returns matched, the vertex numbers, points and normals (mm, current frame), the box round them, centroid and mean normal; fields: count, ids or all (the default) says how much. Trap: at most limit come back (1000 by default, 20000 at most), every k-th spread evenly, step saying k — mark: true marks every matching vertex, not the thinned list, for element.fit_marked { marked: true }. Changes nothing on the part.

box.description: A box in the current frame.

near.description: A ball about a point, in place of box.

normal.description: Only the vertices whose outward normal faces this way.

limit.description: How many vertices at most; 1000 by default, 20000 at most.

mark.description: Leave every matching vertex marked, for element.fit_marked { marked: true }.

fields.description: count: the numbers alone (the default with mark); ids: with the vertices; all: with points and normals (the default).

commands.name: scan.segment
commands.title: Find the scan’s flat regions
commands.description: The scan’s planar regions, found all at once: grown from the flattest places outward within maxDeg (15°) and maxRms (0.05 mm), those smaller than minArea given back. Returns found, considered, claimed, noise and the regions, largest first, at most limit (20): id, normal, point, sigma, area (mm²), box, vertices, neighbours { id, deg, smooth } and, with symmetric, mirror (its twin across that plane). Trap: a round surface comes out as strips that look like facets — such a region says curved { sagitta } and run, and curvedRuns joins them into surfaces with a note saying what to model each as; read the runs before taking regions for faces. mark: a region’s id, or several, leaves their points marked for element.fit_marked { marked: true }. Changes nothing.

kind.description: What to find; plane, the default and for now the only one.

box.description: Only the scan inside this box.

minArea.description: mm²; by default a square 2 % of the scan’s diagonal on a side.

limit.description: How many regions are listed; 20 by default.

symmetric.description: Pair regions mirrored across this plane: a plane element, or "XY", "YZ", "XZ".

oneOf.description: Several regions’ ids, their points together.

mark.description: Leave this region’s points marked, or several regions’.

list.description: With mark: the list of regions too.

commands.name: section.cut
commands.title: Cut a section
commands.description: Cut the scan with a plane and keep the cut as a section, put on the 2D sheet. across: an element with a direction (plane, cylinder, cone, line, circle) by id or name; "XY", "YZ" or "XZ" through the part’s centre; or { axis, angleDeg }, a plane through an axis turned angleDeg about it — a half section of a turned part. offset slides the plane along its normal, mm (a coordinate plane: the coordinate itself). kind "shadow" keeps the scan’s shadow instead: the whole part projected onto the plane, its outer boundary as loops read as lines and arcs (tolerance, play, smoothDeg), stood up as a block for export.step (extrude). Trap: a shadow takes no offset. Returns the section: its plane and chain count — a shadow also its loops, area and band. One undo step.

axis.description: A cylinder, cone, line or circle, or a coordinate axis "X", "Y", "Z".

across.description: An element with a direction, a coordinate plane, or { axis, angleDeg }.

offset.description: Along the normal, mm. A cut’s only.

kind.description: cut (the default), or shadow: the whole scan projected onto the plane.

play.description: Shadow: clearance outside the part, mm; 1 by default, negative a press fit.

tolerance.description: Shadow: lines and arcs read to this, mm; 0.1 by default.

smoothDeg.description: Shadow: corners turning less than this are rounded, degrees; 30 by default, 0 keeps all sharp.

extrude.description: Shadow: stood up as a block through the part, for export.step; true by default.

commands.name: section.get
commands.title: Read a section’s polylines
commands.description: A section’s cut as polylines: each chain’s points in order — [u, v] mm on the sheet, what flat.fit and a sketch on the section take, or with space "world" or "both" [x, y, z] in the current frame — with the plane (origin, normal, basisU, basisV) and per chain closed, length, points, bounds. Trap: at most limit points over all chains (4000 by default, 50000 at most); past it every k-th point is kept and step says k. chains picks chains by index; skin "outer" or "inner" reads one skin of a thin wall alone, facing the points whose way out lies within withinDeg of dir, each chain then coming back as runs. Changes nothing.

section.description: The section, by id or name.

chains.description: Which chains; every one by default.

space.description: sheet (the default): [u, v]; world: [x, y, z]; both.

limit.description: Points at most over every chain; 4000 by default, 50000 at most.

skin.description: One skin of a thin wall alone.

facing.description: Only the points whose way out of the material lies within withinDeg of dir.

commands.name: section.render
commands.title: Picture a section
commands.description: A picture of a section as a PNG, for checking a slice against what was built on it: the scan’s cut as points on the sheet ([u, v] mm, +u right, +v up), a mm grid with values in the margins, a scale bar, and the workspaces’ layers over it (a model’s cut as outlines, a sketch’s pieces). Scan points within ten tolerances of an outline are read against it: on it (grey) or off it (red). Needs section, or plane to cut the scan for the picture alone ({ origin, normal }, "XY"/"YZ"/"XZ", an element, or { sketch }). Returns gap { points, read, over, outside, inside, max, rms, overBox }, layers, axes, sheet (origin, normal, basisU, basisV) and map (pixel (c, r) is [left + c·unitsPerPx, top − r·unitsPerPx]). Trap: a plane’s sheet has its zero at the world origin’s foot, a section’s at the part’s centre — read sheet. 800 px by default, up to 2048. Needs the browser. Changes nothing.

section.description: The section, by id or name.

origin.description: A point on the plane, mm.

plane.description: A plane to cut the scan by for the picture alone, in place of a section.

offsets.description: Several parallel cuts in one picture: mm along the normal — on a coordinate plane by name, from the world’s zero, so "XY" with [0, 5] cuts at Z 0 and Z 5.

up.description: The world axis that runs up the picture; the sheet as it lies by default.

at.description: The middle: [u, v] mm on the sheet, or [x, y, z] mm in the world.

size.description: The side of the square looked at, mm.

world.description: A world box, in place of at and size.

frame.description: Look at a square of the sheet: { at, size }, or { world: { min, max } }.

tolerance.description: ± mm a scan point may lie off an outline and still be on it; the Deviation workspace’s by default.

layers.description: The layers to draw, by key; every one by default, [] for the scan alone.

commands.name: session.recent
commands.title: What recent jobs did
commands.description: What became of the commands an agent’s server ran under its jobs — each change and each batch is one, and the server names it — newest first: the job, the command, running, done or failed, when it started and its ms, and its result or its error { code, message }. A result past 16,000 characters is left out (resultOmitted says its size). The page keeps the last 100 for as long as it stays open, so a server started after the one that asked can still say what a job did. job: only that job’s.

job.description: Only this job’s commands, as the server named it.

limit.description: How many at most, newest first — 20 by default.

commands.name: session.reset
commands.title: Start over
commands.description: Close the scan, the reference part and the 2D image, and with them every measurement and the project’s name, as opening an empty project does. Refuses while the session holds measurements unless discard is true. Not undoable: the history starts over too.

discard.description: true: replace the session though it holds measurements (lost unless saved as a project first). Refused otherwise when there is work to lose.

commands.name: session.state
commands.title: Read the session
commands.description: The whole session as JSON: the app and its plugins, the project (name, unsaved, holds), the workspace on screen, busy, the scan (file, units, counts, bounding box, centre, size, alignment), every element with its fit, every dimension with value, limit and verdict, the sections, what is open in the panels, the deviation, wall thickness and 2D state with their statistics, the guided hint, the undo history and ui.units. Trap: the screen may show inches; every answer here is in millimetres, angles in degrees. Read it before acting and after.

commands.name: thickness.measure
commands.title: Measure the wall thickness
commands.description: Measure the wall thickness at every point of the scan, as the Wall Thickness workspace’s Measure button does, with the search settings given or those in hand. Returns the statistics (min, max, mean, sigma, share under the thin-wall limit, points measured) and the settings. One undo step.

method.description: ray: along the inward normal to the far wall (the shortest of a cone with coneRays). sphere: the largest sphere that fits at the point.

maxThickness.description: The thickest wall searched for, mm.

coneRays.description: ray: rays in the cone about the normal; 0 for the normal alone.

normalDeviationDeg.description: How far the far wall may turn from facing back, degrees, or null for any.

commands.name: thickness.settings
commands.title: Set how the wall thickness is searched and read
commands.description: The search settings (method, maxThickness, coneRays, coneAngleDeg, normalDeviationDeg — they take effect at the next thickness.measure) and the reading: low and high, the ends of the colour scale, mm; bands, a stepped scale or null; limit, the thin-wall limit the statistics count under, mm. Returns the thickness state. One undo step.

method.description: ray: along the inward normal to the far wall (the shortest of a cone with coneRays). sphere: the largest sphere that fits at the point.

maxThickness.description: The thickest wall searched for, mm.

coneRays.description: ray: rays in the cone about the normal; 0 for the normal alone.

normalDeviationDeg.description: How far the far wall may turn from facing back, degrees, or null for any.

commands.name: view.render
commands.title: Picture the view
commands.description: A picture of the 3D view as a PNG — what the viewport shows, without the HTML labels (dimension values, names). view and/or fit turn the view first, as view.set does; frame frames a box or a place (mmAcross says what the picture spans). Trap: only fit: true fits — a view alone keeps the zoom, and a frame stays for the pictures after it (fitted and framedEarlier say so). show puts keys on screen or away for the picture alone ({ scan: false } pictures what was built on the scan); a key that has to be read, a workspace’s map, is waited for up to 35 s, and the answer says how far it got if not; section cuts it open for the picture alone. 800 px on the long side by default, up to 2048; views: two to six standard views in one picture. In the Deviation workspace the answer says which map is painted (map) or why none (mapWhy; mapNote when the reference ghost dulls the colours). Waits for the session to settle. Needs the viewport.

view.description: A standard view: iso (front, right, above) and the other iso corners, top (down Z, Y up), bottom, front (from −Y, Z up), rear, left (from −X), right.

items.description: A standard view: iso (front, right, above) and the other iso corners, top (down Z, Y up), bottom, front (from −Y, Z up), rear, left (from −X), right.

views.description: Several standard views in one picture, each fitted.

fit.description: Fit everything shown into the frame, keeping the direction.

show.description: Keys to show (true) or put away (false): scan, reference, sections, elements (with dimensions), labels, and a workspace’s own (view.set lists every key standing now).

oneOf.description: A box in the current frame, framed whole.

size.description: The side of the square fitted in the picture’s shorter side, mm.

oneOf.description: A place, a square size mm on a side fitted round it.

frame.description: Frame a box or a place instead of everything shown; the direction stays, fit is left alone.

oneOf.description: true: cut square to the view through the part’s middle; false: put it away.

across.description: "XY", "YZ", "XZ", or an element with a direction.

offset.description: Along its normal, mm: a coordinate plane’s coordinate, or from an element’s centre.

flip.description: Take away the far half instead.

section.description: The section view: cut open at a plane, the near half taken away, closed parts capped. Set after any turn.

commands.name: view.set
commands.title: Turn the view
commands.description: Turn the 3D view to a standard view and/or fit everything shown — with neither, it fits — or frame a box or a place; the zoom a frame leaves stays for what comes after. show puts keys on screen or away and leaves them so; section cuts everything open at a plane and leaves it so. Waits for the session to settle first. Not a step of the history. Needs the viewport. Returns view, fitted, framed, framedEarlier, mmAcross ([width, height] mm), section (null when off) and shown: every key and whether it is, with <key>Why for a workspace key that is off.

view.description: A standard view: iso (front, right, above) and the other iso corners, top (down Z, Y up), bottom, front (from −Y, Z up), rear, left (from −X), right.

fit.description: Fit everything shown into the frame, keeping the direction.

show.description: Keys to show (true) or put away (false): scan, reference, sections, elements (with dimensions), labels, and a workspace’s own (view.set lists every key standing now).

oneOf.description: A box in the current frame, framed whole.

size.description: The side of the square fitted in the picture’s shorter side, mm.

oneOf.description: A place, a square size mm on a side fitted round it.

frame.description: Frame a box or a place instead of everything shown; the direction stays, fit is left alone.

oneOf.description: true: cut square to the view through the part’s middle; false: put it away.

across.description: "XY", "YZ", "XZ", or an element with a direction.

offset.description: Along its normal, mm: a coordinate plane’s coordinate, or from an element’s centre.

flip.description: Take away the far half instead.

section.description: The section view: cut open at a plane, the near half taken away, closed parts capped. Set after any turn.

commands.name: workspace.set
commands.title: Show a workspace
commands.description: Put a workspace on screen: measure (fitting elements and dimensions), deviation (scan against a reference part or an element), thickness (wall thickness), flat (2D measuring of an image or a section), or a plugin’s by its id — session.state lists them under app.plugins. Commands put their own workspace on screen; this is for showing the person something.

workspace.description: The workspace — measure, deviation, thickness, flat, or a plugin’s id.
